Conformal inference (CI) is a data-efficient method for formally providing guarantees on
the δ-quantile of distributions. This method involves sampling an i.i.d. scalar dataset, sorting
the samples in ascending order, and demonstrating that one of the sorted samples represents
the δ-quantile. The integration of CI with formal verification techniques has recently received
noticeable interest, that is primarily due to its accuracy and level of scalability. For instance,
Bortolussi et al. (2019) merges CI with neural state classifiers to develop a stochastic runtime
verification algorithm. Lindemann et al. (2023); Zecchin et al. (2024) employ CI to guarantee
safety in MPC control using a trained model. Tonkens et al. (2023) applies CI for planning
with probabilistic safety guarantees, and Hashemi et al. (2024b) integrates CI with existing
neural network reachability techniques and provides a scalable reachability analysis on
stochastic systems, see Lindemann et al. (2024) for a recent survey article.
